To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
chemokines and in particular eotaxins are potent regulators of allergic lung inflammation and that IL-13 is a key cytokine in the regulation of eotaxin expression.

1) IL-13 is a potent regulator of the asthmatics response, 2) chemokines are critical regulators of the asthmaticeosinophilic response, 3) chemokines and eotaxins are potent activators of TH2 cells, and 4) IL-13 and eotaxin cooperate in promoting the asthmatic inflammatory response.
chemokines and in particular eotaxins promote IL-13-mediated allergic responses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of asthma and allergic inflammation.
understanding the mechanisms by which chemokines, and particularly eotaxins and their receptors, regulate IL-13-mediated allergic responses.
understanding the mechanisms of asthma and the potential for novel therapies to treat asthma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chemokines are important mediators in asthma and that chemokines and chemokine receptors are attractive targets for the treatment and prevention of asthma.
chemokines are critical mediators in the pathogenesis, and IL-13 is a critical mediator in the pathogenesis and progression of asthma.
chemokines and chemokine receptors play an essential role in the pathogenesis and maintenance of asthma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chemokine eotaxin-1 is a critical mediator of the IL-13-dependent allergic response.
chemokines and cytokines are important in the development of asthma.
IL-13 and eotaxin have an important synergistic role in the pathogenesis and maintenance of allergic lung responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chemokines are not just a bystander in the asthmatics response.
chemokines are critical mediators of allergic disease and that IL-13 and eotaxins are central regulators of the allergic response.

chemokines and eotaxins in particular, are critical regulators of IL-13-induced allergic lung disease, and that pharmacological targeting of these pathways may provide a novel and effective therapeutic approach for the treatment of asthma.
